I'm here in opposition to the Iron Horse Data Center proposal and to urge caution and restraint in your consideration and deliberations for this proposed site. The proliferation of data center proposals in Virginia and in Hanover County in particular are bringing into clear focus issues regarding power, water usage, and pollution with respect to noise, air, and water. I find it hard to believe that these projects are moving forward without more state and local guidelines in place. Just this past week, Governor Spanberg reissued

her data center accountability framework to lay out some reasonable steps with regard to transparency, protecting the environment, lowering energy costs, and prioritizing people. This will be taken up by the General Assembly in the coming year. At the local level, this body formed a committee to examine the pros and cons surrounding the data center issue.

That effort is projected to take 12 to 18 months to complete. While these foundational efforts are commendable, the rules and guidelines that will be generated will nevertheless be coming years too late if Iron Horse is approved.

I believe this guidance should have been in place long before soliciting and considering data center development proposals from developers. County guidelines need to address the cumulative connection of data centers to the grid, the power, and the many impacts on air quality, water supply, electric bills, and people and communities who live here in Hanover County.

There isn't just local opposition anymore. State senators from both parties are now calling for a statewide moratorium on new data center approval until Virginia knows whether its water and power systems can actually accommodate them.

If state leaders are saying we need to pause and take stock, you should not be recommending new capacity before the question can be answered with any degree of certainty. The Iron Horse proposal is tenuous at best. The project has already been deferred twice, including one time an hour before its own hearing.

A project this size with unresolved water, sewer, power grid, and environmental and pollution impacts deserves complete answers before a vote. and not a promise for recommendation that assumes the required answers will be made available.
